newsitem.title: USA: Henkel, analysts' EPS views close - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Henkel, analysts' EPS views close - CEO.

text.p: German chemical company Henkel KGaA and analysts have similar estimates for the company's 1997 earnings per share, president and chief executive Hans-Dietrich Winkhaus said Monday.
He told a news conference that analysts' average estimate for earnings per share this year was 4.35 marks.
"The estimate for 1997 done by analysts are not far from our own internal" estimates, Winkhaus said.
He added that, based on Henkel's performance in the first quarter, "we are optimistic we can increase our profits compared to 1996." He did not provide detailed figures.
Henkel reported record 1996 net earnings of 515 million marks on sales of 16.3 billion marks.

Winkhaus said key company efforts in 1997 included expanding Henkel's presence in China, restructuring its chemical products sector and absorbing the purchase of U.S. adhesives maker Loctite Corp LOC.N.
In China, Henkel wants to increase the number of detergent brands it sells and markets, including Chinese brands, and introduce its own signature Persil mark.
The company also is focusing on such items as hair coloring and skin care products in China. Winkhaus said Henkel was in an "investment phase" of developing the Chinese market.

Henkel plans to restructure its chemical products sector to increase profitability. In part the company will aim to become a low-cost producer of oleochemicals, used in cosmetics and detergents and vitamin E and aroma chemicals.

"In addition, we want to concentrate on specialties for the cosmetics industry, on new high-quality surfactants such as APG (alcylpolyglycoside), on food additives and on antioxidants like vitamin E," Winkhaus said.
Surfactants are used in such items as soap or detergents for treatment of surfaces.

Winkhaus said initial decisions had already been made about integrating Loctite into Henkel's international structure. Henkel completed in January its $1.3 billion purchase of the 65 percent of Loctite it did not already own.

David Freeman, president and chief executive of Loctite, said any layoffs arising from the acquisition likely would take place among sales and marketing staff in Europe. About half of Loctite's 4,500 employees work in marketing and sales.

Winkhaus also said the company had not made a decision whether or not to trade Henkel's shares publicly on the New York Stock Exchange as American Depositary Receipts (ADRs). The ADRs now trade over the counter among the pink sheets.
